what: Frequency of Bash tool_use commands issued by every Claude Code session (coordinator and subagents) that ran against this repository, normalized to the first one-to-three tokens of each subcommand of a compound command. Used to pick which read-only commands go into .claude/settings.json permissions.allow, ranked by measured pain rather than guesswork.
source: Every *.jsonl transcript under ~/.claude/projects/C--gamedev-Dungeon-fortress/ as of 2026-08-07 — both top-level session transcripts and the subagents/agent-*.jsonl transcripts nested under each session directory (coordinator delegates most Bash calls to subagents, so excluding them would undercount). tool-results/*.txt files in the same tree are not JSONL and are excluded by the *.jsonl filter.

scope.note: 13358 counted by taking the first line of each Bash call's input.command (jq 'split("\n")[0]'); an independent per-file object count (jq '[...] | length') gives 13365 — the 7-call gap is a handful of files where a stray line failed to parse and were silently skipped by the `2>/dev/null` in the loop below. Not re-investigated: 0.05% of the total, does not move any ranking used below.

stage1_extractFirstLineOfEachBashCommand: while IFS= read -r f; do jq -r '.message.content[]? | select(.type=="tool_use" and .name=="Bash") | (.input.command // "") | split("\n")[0]' "$f" 2>/dev/null; done < files.txt > commands_firstline.txt
command.stage1Rationale: input.command can be a multi-line heredoc/script. A first pass that used jq -r '...| .input.command' directly (no split) produced one text line per newline inside the command, which silently multiplied heredoc-heavy commands (e.g. gh pr comment --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)") and inflated their apparent frequency. split("\n")[0] keeps exactly one record per Bash call, which is what 'frequency of a command' has to mean.
command.stage2Rationale: 92.8% of raw Bash calls (12402/13358) started with a literal 'cd' because the repo's own convention is `cd <worktree-or-repo-path> && <real command>` (see CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md worktree rules). A naive first-token count would have shown 'cd' as the dominant command and buried git/gh/rg under it. Splitting each call on the shell separators && || ; | and counting every resulting subcommand segment (dropping bare 'cd ...' segments, since cd is not the command being confirmed) recovers the actual command mix. git and gh get 2-3 token keys (git status, gh pr view) because the subcommand, not the verb alone, is what determines read-only-ness; every other tool is keyed on its first token alone (rg, fd, wc, ...), matching the issue's own examples.
command.caveatCompoundJqFilters: A `--jq '.foo | .bar'` argument to gh contains a literal '|' that this naive splitter treats as a shell pipe, producing a handful of spurious low-count segments (e.g. '.bar' as a fake command). This is visible only in the long tail (counts of 1-3) and never affects any command in the allowlist below or its ranking.

consideredAndExcluded.excludedBecause: network call; issue #286 non-goals restrict network access to read-only 'gh ... view/list', git fetch does not qualify even though it does not touch the working tree

blanket prefix would also allow 'git worktree add/remove/prune', which create/delete worktrees and branches; 68% of observed calls are exactly those writing subcommands, so a narrower 'git worktree list' rule was considered but dropped to keep the checkpoint scope to the issue's named examples
blanket prefix would also allow 'git branch -D' (delete branch); 32 of 161 observed calls are -D
not read-only: switches branches and can discard uncommitted changes ('git checkout -- <path>')

the real subcommand sits after -C and is not captured by prefix matching on 'git -C'; would need a pattern per subcommand ('git -C * status', ...) not attempted in this pass — named as a follow-up gap, not fixed here
